The SIRS module for the XH component

Source: R/host-xde-SIRS.R
SIRS.Rd

Implements the XH component using a Susceptible-Infectious-Recovered-Susceptible (SIRS) compartmental model of human infection dynamics, extending SIR with waning immunity so that recovered individuals return to the susceptible class. This implementation includes human demographic change and support for progressive stratification.

State Variables

H

total human (or host) population density

I

density of infectious humans

R

density of recovered (temporarily immune) humans

S=H-I-R

density of susceptible humans or hosts

Dynamical Term

\(h\) or foi

The force of infection is computed and stored by Exposure as FoI

A constant fraction of infectious bites causes an infection: the parameter \(b\).

Parameters

make_XH_obj_SIRS supplies defaults for the parameters, which can be changed using change_XH_pars.SIRS.

b

transmission probability from mosquito to human

c

transmission probability from human to mosquito

r

clearance rate for infections

gamma

rate of waning immunity (loss of \(R\))

Infection Dynamics

Susceptible individuals become infectious at rate \(hS\). Infections clear at the per-capita rate \(r\), moving individuals into the recovered class. Immunity wanes at rate \(\gamma\), returning recovered individuals to susceptibility. $$ \begin{array}{rl} dI/dt &= hS - rI - \mathbf{D}(I) \\ dR/dt &= rI - \gamma R - \mathbf{D}(R) \\ \end{array}$$ where \(h\) is the force of infection and \(S = H - I - R\). The mortality function uses the same model for \(I\) and \(R\) as for \(H\). Susceptible density is redundant and is computed after solving.

Prevalence

F_prevalence.SIRS returns \(x=I/H\). This module has no diagnostic sensitivity parameters or module-specific light microscopy, RDT, or PCR prevalence methods.

Infectiousness

The probability that a mosquito becomes infected after feeding on an infectious host is \(c\). Infectious density is \(cI\), and net infectiousness is \(cI/H\).

Mass Treatment

This implementation does not initialize or use mda(t) or msat(t), and has no treatment parameters rho or sigma.

Demography

This model has no parameter or terms to describe disease-induced mortality.

Births or \(\mathbf{B}\)

the births function

Deaths or \(\mathbf{D}\)

the deaths function

Setup:

The default is a constant population model: birth and death rates are set to zero

  • Use setup_births to configure Births

  • Use setup_deaths to configure Deaths

Also, see xds_info_demographic_change.
